Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Ikran\AppData\Local\Temp\f52\put-green\skills\relay-morpheus

# relay-morpheus — staged runs that outlive the session

A staged run has two records. The transcript, which dies with the session, and
the tree, which does not. Everything that matters has to be in the second one
**while the run is still going**, because there is no guarantee you reach the
end to write it down.

## The rule

```
WRITE THE STAGE DOWN BEFORE YOU DISPATCH IT, NOT AFTER IT COMES BACK
```

This is the one thing this skill exists for, and it is the one thing three
isolated baseline runs did not do (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-morpheus.txt`).
All three executed a four-stage plan end to end and left no on-disk record of
progress until the very last write — one left none at all. A session ending
anywhere before that leaves a working tree full of unattributed diff and no way
to tell which stages produced it, which were finished, or what was still
running.

Reading a mid-run tree is **not** this skill's problem. The companion baseline
(`scenario-relay-morpheus-resume.txt`) shows a fresh session doing that correctly
unprompted, against pressure to trust stale checkboxes. Relay adds nothing
there and says nothing about it.

**Violating the letter of this is violating the spirit of it.** "I'll record it
when the stage returns" is the failure, not a variation on it — the stages that
need recording most are the ones that never return.

## Handing a run to another session

Every run gets a short number when it is created, and `init` prints the
sentence that resumes it:

```
hand this to any session:  continue RUN-0003
```

That sentence is the whole interface. A fresh session — another machine,
another host, a colleague — needs nothing else: **"continue RUN-0003"**. It has no
transcript, so the ledger is what it reads, and the ledger is on disk because
it was written before the work, not after.

```sh
relay-morpheus.sh list          # every run, what is open, and its resume sentence
relay-morpheus.sh resume 3      # everything a session that has never seen it needs
relay-morpheus.sh 3 status      # any command takes the id first
```

**One name, everywhere (F44).** A run is `RUN-0003`: its serial number,
zero-padded to four digits (more past 9999, never cut). That one name is the run
file (`run-0003-<slug>.md`), its `# RUN-0003` header, its branch and worktree,
its queue row and the resume sentence. `RUN-0003`, `RUN-3`, `run-3` and `3` all
resolve to the same run, because whoever types it next is working from memory
of a conversation rather than from a path - and a run named before F44
(`run-3-*.md`, `# RUN-3`) is found by every spelling too, and listed padded.
With one run open and no id given, that run is assumed; with two or more, the
script refuses rather than guessing.

**Run owners (F44).** A run can be given to a team member: `relay-morpheus.sh
[<id>] owner @asha` (`-Mode owner [-Id n] -Text @asha`) writes an `owner: @asha`
line in the run file's header, `owner -` clears it, and `init --owner @asha`
(`-RunOwner @asha`) sets it at the start. Handles come from tickets-zordon's
`.skillator/team.md` (`- @asha: asha@x.com`); a handle not in it is refused, and
with no team file any well-formed `@handle` is taken, with a note. `list`,
`resume`, `status` and `queue-run list` show the owner.

## The run file

`.skillator/run-<0000>-<slug>.md`, one per run, in the repo. Markdown because a human and any
host both have to read it with no tooling. Git-tracked by default; a repo that
objects can `.gitignore` it and lose only the shared view, not the resume.

```markdown
# RUN-0007 — notekeep v2
plan: docs/plans/PLAN-notekeep.md
started: 2026-09-22T09:14Z   updated: 2026-09-22T10:02Z
owner: @asha

## Stages
| # | stage | state | owner | heartbeat | landed |
|---|-------|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 41 | list --json     | x | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T09:22Z | 3f1a2c9 |
| 42 | tags + --tag    | ~ | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T10:02Z | - |
| 43 | export          |   | -            | -     | - |
| 44 | README          |   | -            | -     | - |

## In flight
### stage 42 — tags + --tag  (dispatched 09:51)
prompt: |
  Add a `tags` list to each note in notekeep/store.py and a `list --tag <t>`
  filter in notekeep/cli.py. Test both. Do not touch export or the README.
last seen: wrote store.py, tests not yet run.

## Rulings
- 09:38 — stage 41 emits `[]` not `null` for an empty store — the plan does not
  say, JSON consumers expect a list — costs a one-line change if wrong.
```

**States:** `` (pending) · `~` in flight · `x` landed · `!` failed · `?`
parked (chain only: every item waits on a decision) · `>` re-planned (`landed`
names the new stage).
**`landed`** is a commit sha or a path, never a claim. An empty `landed` on an
`x` row is a lie the next session will believe.
**One run, one worktree (F35).** In a git repo with a commit, `init` also
creates the run's own worktree, `<repo>/.skillator/worktrees/RUN-0007-<slug>`
(git-ignored, inside the repo so dispatched agents may work there), on
branch `run/RUN-0007-<slug>`, and writes both into the run file's header. Every
stage of the run works and commits **there** - say so in each dispatch prompt -
never in the main checkout, whose index another run may be using. The run
file itself stays in the main checkout's `.skillator/`, whichever worktree
calls the script. `resume` names the worktree and recreates it from its branch
if it is gone. `init --here` (`-Here`) keeps the old one-checkout behaviour.
The run reaches main through its final stage: merge `run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` from
the main checkout, then `git worktree remove <worktree>` and
`git branch -d run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` - nothing removes them for you.
**Leases across runs (F36).** `chain dispatch` leases the stage's `files:` in
one registry per clone (`<git-common-dir>/skillator/leases`); a file another
run's live stage holds refuses the dispatch (`LEASED <path> RUN-m stage s`,
exit 2) and `chain next` shows the stage `IDLE ... leased`. Landing, failing
or re-planning releases; a lease silent past 20 min is taken, with a ruling.
Board edits from a run worktree go through `relay-morpheus.sh board <ID>
<mark>` (`-Mode board -Ticket -Mark`), which writes the main checkout's
`TICKETS.md` under its lock.
**Parallel stages (F37).** `chain next --all` names every stage that can run
now - files disjoint from what is in flight and from each other - capped at 2
below 50 % of the 5-hour window, else 1. A stage that runs beside another works
in its own worktree off the run branch; `chain merge <n>` brings it back (exit
3 on a conflict: the stage fails). [references/chain.md](references/chain.md).
**A marathon of runs (F38).** Runs wait in one queue (`queue-run add|next|
start|pause|done`), run one at a time, and land on main one at a time
(`land <n> --start`, review and bump on the run branch, `land <n> --finish`);
one end batch across runs (`queue --all`), one push per marathon, and an away
flow (`away on|off`) that notifies, waits 30 minutes and moves on - never a
default. [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md).
**Numbers are serial across the project, not per run.** `init` takes the RUN
id and every stage number from the F21 allocator (`practice/scripts/next-id.sh`,
kinds `RUN` and `S`), which reads every run file in the tree and on every ref
and keeps a counter every worktree of the clone shares — so two worktrees never
both make RUN-4, and a new run's first stage continues after the highest stage
any run has used (RUN-0007 above starts at 41). "Stage 42" names one stage in the
whole project. Existing run files are never renumbered.
**Rulings** are appended, never rewritten — see `tasks-sentinels`, which is
where they come from and which writes into this same file.

## The loop

1. **Before dispatch** — add or update the stage row to `~`, write the In-flight
   block with the *exact prompt you are about to send*, stamp the heartbeat.
   Prompt not written down → the agent is not recoverable → do not dispatch.
2. **While it runs** — re-stamp the heartbeat whenever the agent reports. A
   stale heartbeat is the only signal you get that a network drop took it;
   `hooks/relay-morpheus.* orphans` turns that into a list.
3. **When it lands** — commit the stage's work, then set `x` and put the sha in
   `landed`, and delete its In-flight block. In that order: the sha cannot be
   written before the commit exists.
4. **When it fails** — `!`, and leave the In-flight block where it is with the
   failure appended. A failed stage's prompt is the thing you need most.
5. **Never** delete a row. A run file only grows.

Stages that touch the same files do not run at once; independent ones do
(`PRACTICE.md` §4). Either way each gets its row before it gets its agent.

## Resuming

Open `.skillator/run.md`, then check it against the tree — the file is written
before the work, so the last `~` row is a stage that *started*, not one that
finished. `landed` shas are ground truth; anything else is a claim to verify.
Redispatch straight from the stored prompt; the rows are keyed by stage number,
so a redispatch that duplicates work overwrites rather than appends.

Then carry on. A resume does not need permission to continue — see
`grayskull-power` §3, **run to the end**.

## Chaining ticket workflows

When the stages are ticket workflows that start each other — "work every open
ticket in staged workflows, keep going" — the rule above gains a second half:

```
THE NEXT STAGE IS STARTED BY THE LAST ONE'S COMPLETION, AND BY NOTHING
ELSE UNTIL USAGE SAYS SO
```

Two isolated runs (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-chain*.txt`) dispatched
with no plan on disk, read no usage between stages, named stages by their
content (two runs picked the same name), and started a stage at 84 % of the
5-hour window. So a chain is run **only** by the loop in
[references/chain.md](references/chain.md): every stage `chain plan`ned with
its code and exact prompt before the first dispatch; `chain decide` (on
`usage-watch level`) before every stage, the first included; `chain hold` at 80 % and a `chain wait` listener instead
of a new stage; `mode:` in the run file naming what was actually dispatched.
Read that file before the first `chain` command.

Every chain is a **marathon**: a question only the user can answer is parked
on disk (`park`), the chain goes on with every stage that does not wait on it
(`chain next`), and the queue is asked once, at the end. The six stops are
never parked:

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION -
NEVER AS ONE ITEM OF THE END BATCH
```

Two baseline runs (`scenario-marathon-stop.txt`) left an untracked directory
alone, said its deletion could not be undone, and then asked it as item 2 of 3
beside a format question. Read [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md)
when a verdict carries `parked`, a stop fires, or `chain next` prints `ASK` or
`UNBLOCK`.

## Scripts

`hooks/relay-morpheus.sh` · `hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1` — the same commands, mirrored per
`PLATFORMS.md`: `init`, `add`, `stage`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `orphans`, and
`chain plan|dispatch|hold|release|wait|status|decide|next|edge`, and the
marathon's `park`, `answer`, `queue`. They are
bookkeeping, not judgement; every one reads or edits `.skillator/run.md` and
nothing else. Run `selftest` on both after touching either.
`watchdog hold "<why>" | release | status` (F48, the ops-board mod on red disk/memory) holds every new `chain dispatch` and GREEN harness `run`, exit 2, until released.
`chain decide --level "<level line>"` (F49) decides on a reading the caller already has.

```sh
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  init plan.md "notekeep v2" "list --json" "tags" "export" "README"
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  add "docs pass"                    # a stage found mid-run; prints 45
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 '~' build:sonnet          # before you dispatch
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 x  build:sonnet 3f1a2c9   # after you commit
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  orphans 20                         # who has gone quiet
```

```powershell
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode init  -Plan plan.md -Title "notekeep v2" -Stages "list --json,tags,export,README"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode add   -Title "docs pass"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State '~' -Owner build:sonnet
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State x   -Owner build:sonnet -Landed 3f1a2c9
# In a headless or nested run on Windows, call the .sh through the Bash tool:
# the PowerShell tool refuses `& <script>.ps1` and `powershell -File` under any
# allow rule (A91, claude 2.1.280).
```

Add rows with `add`, never by hand: a hand-typed number is the per-run
restart this numbering removed. The scripts find the allocator beside the
installed skills (`<skills>/practice/scripts/`, or `<root>/practice/scripts/`
in a clone or the plugin cache; `RELAY_NEXT_ID` overrides). Without it they
fall back to the old local rule and say so on stderr — numbers then repeat
across worktrees.

Three constraints the pair has to keep, each learned the hard way:

- **Pure ASCII, and the empty cell is `-`, not an em dash.** Windows PowerShell
  5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI and corrupts anything above 126.
- **The run file is LF with no BOM, written to a temp and moved.** Both mirrors
  edit the same file, so one of them flipping encoding rewrites every line in
  the diff; and a kill between truncate and write would empty the only record
  of what was in flight.
- **`-Stages` takes `"a,b,c"` and pending is spelled `pending`.** PowerShell's
  `-File` passes each argument as one literal string and drops empty ones, and
  `-File` is how every hook here invokes it.

### Seeing a run without being told about one

`list` prints every run with its resume sentence, and prints nothing when there
are none, so it is safe as a `SessionStart` hook. With one wired, a session that inherits
a half-finished run sees it in its own context before the user has to remember
to mention it — which is the difference between resuming and starting over.

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1\" -Mode list",
  "timeout": 5
} ] } ] } }
```

macOS/Linux: `sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh list`. Forward slashes throughout —
PowerShell accepts them and it removes all backslash-escaping from the JSON.
Other hosts have no equivalent event; there, reading `.skillator/run.md` is the
first thing `resume-cortana` does. `watch-cortana` already drains in-flight
agents at the limit — relay is what it drains *into*, so the two do not overlap.

1	# Chaining ticket workflows — the procedure
2	
3	A chain is a relay run whose stages are ticket workflows, each started by the
4	previous one's completion notification. Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-relay-chain.md`.
5	The commands below are `hooks/relay-morpheus.sh chain …` (PowerShell:
6	`relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode chain -Action … -N …`); `RM` stands for
7	`sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh`, `UW` for
8	`sh <skills>/watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh`. They are page shorthand only:
9	type the full `sh "<path>" …` every time, never `RM=…; $RM …` — Claude Code's
10	permission check refuses a command whose variable it cannot read (seen in the
11	F31 GREEN run).
12	
13	## When it applies
14	
15	The user asks to work the open tickets as a sequence of workflows — "work every
16	open ticket in staged workflows", "keep going on your own", "auto-start the next
17	workflow", "next stage" — or a resume lands on a run file with a `## Chain`
18	section. A board of 1-3 tickets is `tickets-zordon` plain dispatch, not a chain.
19	
20	## Step 1 — plan from the board (main session, before anything is dispatched)
21	
22	```sh
23	grep -nE '^\s*- \[[ ~!]\]' TICKETS.md
24	```
25	
26	1. `[ ]` and `[~]` go in. A `[~]` stamped by another session's tag is skipped
27	   with a ruling. `[>]` is never planned and never re-checked.
28	2. `[!]` rows: read `(blocked: …)`. Names a ticket that is now `[x]`, or a
29	   file/condition the tree satisfies (check the tree, not the text) → flip it
30	   to `[ ]` and put it in a **later** stage than what unblocked it. Otherwise
31	   leave it out and say so. `(blocked: RUN-n Qk)` resolves only when Qk is
32	   `replanned` or `moot` (`RM chain status` shows `## Decisions`).
33	3. Name the files per ticket (ticket text plus one grep). Same-file tickets are
34	   one item or different stages — never two agents in one stage.
35	4. Tier each ticket per seat (`tickets-zordon` table): `A110 deep/build`.
36	5. One stage = one Workflow call, at most six items, ordered by dependency
37	   then age. The last stage is always `verify review bump commit push`, owned
38	   by the main session. A stage that needs another's output gets `--after <n>`.
39	6. A ticket whose spec leaves a user-owned choice open → `RM park` it now
40	   ([marathon.md](marathon.md), Park); it joins no stage until answered.
41	
42	Write every stage to the run file, then plan every work stage with its exact
43	prompt, **before the first dispatch**:
44	
45	```sh
46	RM init TICKETS.md "drain the board" "B2+B3 books" "F2+F5 report, F3 cli" "verify review bump commit push"
47	printf '%s\n' "<the exact per-item prompts the script will send>" > .skillator/chain-66.txt
48	RM chain plan 66 --tickets "B2,B3" --fix build --verify build --files shelf/books.py --prompt-file .skillator/chain-66.txt
49	```
50	
51	`init` printed the run's worktree (`stages work and commit in: ...`): every
52	prompt file says "work and commit in <worktree> (branch run/RUN-<n>-...),
53	never in the main checkout", and pastes this paragraph verbatim (A126 - a
54	background agent cannot ask for approval, so a command shape the host gates
55	is simply lost):
56	
57	> In the worktree, run one plain command per call, by absolute path - never
58	> `cd` (or `Set-Location`) into it first. Git: `git -C "<worktree>" status`,
59	> `git -C "<worktree>" add <paths>`, `git -C "<worktree>" commit -m "..."`.
60	> Tests: `python -m pytest "<worktree>/tests"` (or the project's runner with
61	> the worktree path as its argument). No `&&` chains, no `$(...)`, no heredocs;
62	> read and edit files with the file tools, not shell redirection. The final stage merges that branch into main
63	from the main checkout, then removes the worktree and the branch. A `LEASED`
64	refusal (exit 2) means another run's stage holds one of this stage's files:
65	`chain next` lists it `IDLE <n> leased ...`; dispatch something else and come
66	back after that run lands. Ticket boxes are flipped with `RM board <ID> <mark>`
67	- the main checkout's board, under its lock.
68	
69	`chain plan` allocates the 4-character code (`next-id.sh --runs .skillator W`),
70	prefixes it to the stage cell, and appends a block under `## Chain`. It refuses
71	without a prompt file and never reissues a code. Repeat for each work stage;
72	the final main-session stage needs no block. Without a Workflow tool, add
73	`--mode agents`.
74	
75	Print the plan once — stages, codes, tickets, tiers, agent count, tickets left
76	out and why. A request that said "work the board in stages / keep going" is
77	the opt-in; "plan" stops here. No "shall I continue?" afterwards.
78	
79	## Step 2 — dispatch a stage
80	
81	Read usage first — before **every** dispatch, the first one included. A
82	reading the user gave in the prompt counts too; the higher of the two wins:
83	
84	```sh
85	RM chain decide   # HOLD <pct> → step 4 now, dispatch nothing; RELEASE → go on
86	RM chain dispatch 66 --driver @cc-<6 chars of this session id> --owner build:opus
87	```
88	
89	`dispatch` reads usage itself too. It refuses (exit 2) while `hold:` is set,
90	at or over the 5-hour hold without `--override` (the user asked; a ruling),
91	past the 7-day stop without `--confirmed`, while another driver's stamp is
92	under 20 minutes old (`--take` overrides, with a ruling), and on a stage that
93	is not pending or failed. `UNOBSERVABLE` dispatches, with a one-line note on
94	stderr. The checks and the claim are one lock hold: two sessions dispatching
95	one stage get one winner and one exit 2. On success it sets the row `~`,
96	copies the planned prompt verbatim into an In-flight block, and prints the code
97	and the prompt. Then:
98	
99	1. Flip the stage's tickets to `[~]` with the session tag; grep them back.
100	2. Call `Workflow` with the `work-tickets` script shape from `tickets-zordon`;
101	   every fix and verify prompt carries the marathon.md paste-in paragraph,
102	   and the VERDICT schema its `parked` field.
103	   `meta.name: 'chain-<CODE>'`, every agent `label: '<CODE> fix:B2'` /
104	   `'<CODE> verify:B2'`, `args` = the items with tiers. **An F ticket's item is
105	   a `build-jarvis` pass** (F39), not a bare fix agent: its prompt opens with
106	   "Load skillator:build-jarvis" and the ticket, and build-jarvis grades,
107	   designs and builds it - B and A tickets keep the fix/verify shape.
108	3. Edit the In-flight block's `run: -` to the `runId` the tool returned — no
109	   command fills it. The prompt on disk is the truth; the id is a same-session
110	   hint for `resumeFromRunId`.
111	
112	**Several in flight (F37).** `RM chain next --all` prints one `NEXT` line per
113	stage that can start now - its after: stages landed, its files disjoint from
114	every stage in flight and from the others it names, held by no decision and no
115	other run's lease - capped by usage: 2 below 50 % of the 5-hour window, 1 at or
116	above it or unobservable (`RELAY_CHAIN_PARALLEL` overrides). Dispatch each
117	(one dispatch and one Workflow/Agent call per stage). A stage left out says
118	why: `IDLE <n> slots`, `IDLE <n> parallel-files <m>`, `IDLE <n> inflight-files
119	<m>`; dispatch refuses a stage that shares files with one in flight, and one
120	with no `files:` never runs beside anything. A stage dispatched while another
121	is in flight gets its own worktree off the run branch - dispatch says so on
122	stderr and writes `worktree:`/`branch:` into its In-flight block; its prompt
123	must say to work and commit there. Each stage is landed by Step 3 when **its
124	own** notification arrives - the others keep running - and before its `stage x`
125	run `RM chain merge <n>`: it merges the stage branch into the run branch and
126	removes the stage worktree. Exit 3 is a conflict: the merge is aborted, the
127	stage is `!`, and a retry stage is planned on the merged branch. Then
128	`chain next --all` again fills the free slots.
129	`chain next --holds` (A118) prints only the `IDLE <n> Qk <why>` lines and
130	writes nothing - no lease beat, no lock - for readers such as holo-r2d2.
131	
132	`mode:` in the Chain header names what actually ran: `workflow` for a Workflow
133	call, `agents` for Agent fan-out. A run file that says `workflow` while Agents
134	were used is a lie the next session believes — fix it with
135	`RM chain plan … --mode agents` at planning time, or by editing the header.
136	
137	## Step 3 — between stages (the completion notification is the event)
138	
139	Run every line, in order, before the next dispatch:
140	
141	1. Read the returned array; read `<transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl` before
142	   believing an empty one. `null` → ticket stays `[~]`, said in the ruling.
143	   `passed:false` → `[ ]` with the `why` on the line. `passed:true` → `[x]`
144	   only when the evidence names a check that ran. The main session flips the
145	   board; no agent does. A verdict with `parked` → marathon.md (Park) first:
146	   `RM park` before anything else; `parked.stop` not `none` is a stop, now.
147	2. Regression sweep, then `code-review:code-review` on the staged diff; fix
148	   findings via a fix agent (3-pass cap). Usage pressure lowers the level,
149	   never the call: `/code-review low` is the floor. Reading the diff yourself
150	   is not a review - "to save usage I reviewed it myself" lands nothing.
151	3. Commit with the ticket-first message and the code trailing:
152	   `B2 B3: <what> [<CODE>]`. No review result from step 2, no `x`: the stage
153	   stays `~`. Then `RM stage 66 x build:opus <sha>` and delete
154	   the stage's In-flight block by hand (no command does). No passing ticket →
155	   `RM stage 66 '!'`, block kept with the failure appended, chain continues;
156	   one retry stage per ticket via `RM add`.
157	4. Republish the board artifact once (`tickets-zordon`).
158	5. `Ruling:` line — `<CODE>: <what the verdicts decided, what was dropped>;
159	   review <level>: <n> findings, <fixed|none>`.
160	6. Usage read, every stage, no exception:
161	
162	   ```sh

# Chaining ticket workflows — the procedure

A chain is a relay run whose stages are ticket workflows, each started by the
previous one's completion notification. Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-relay-chain.md`.
The commands below are `hooks/relay-morpheus.sh chain …` (PowerShell:
`relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode chain -Action … -N …`); `RM` stands for
`sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh`, `UW` for
`sh <skills>/watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh`. They are page shorthand only:
type the full `sh "<path>" …` every time, never `RM=…; $RM …` — Claude Code's
permission check refuses a command whose variable it cannot read (seen in the
F31 GREEN run).

## When it applies

The user asks to work the open tickets as a sequence of workflows — "work every
open ticket in staged workflows", "keep going on your own", "auto-start the next
workflow", "next stage" — or a resume lands on a run file with a `## Chain`
section. A board of 1-3 tickets is `tickets-zordon` plain dispatch, not a chain.

## Step 1 — plan from the board (main session, before anything is dispatched)

```sh
grep -nE '^\s*- \[[ ~!]\]' TICKETS.md
```

1. `[ ]` and `[~]` go in. A `[~]` stamped by another session's tag is skipped
   with a ruling. `[>]` is never planned and never re-checked.
2. `[!]` rows: read `(blocked: …)`. Names a ticket that is now `[x]`, or a
   file/condition the tree satisfies (check the tree, not the text) → flip it
   to `[ ]` and put it in a **later** stage than what unblocked it. Otherwise
   leave it out and say so. `(blocked: RUN-n Qk)` resolves only when Qk is
   `replanned` or `moot` (`RM chain status` shows `## Decisions`).
3. Name the files per ticket (ticket text plus one grep). Same-file tickets are
   one item or different stages — never two agents in one stage.
4. Tier each ticket per seat (`tickets-zordon` table): `A110 deep/build`.
5. One stage = one Workflow call, at most six items, ordered by dependency
   then age. The last stage is always `verify review bump commit push`, owned
   by the main session. A stage that needs another's output gets `--after <n>`.
6. A ticket whose spec leaves a user-owned choice open → `RM park` it now
   ([marathon.md](marathon.md), Park); it joins no stage until answered.

Write every stage to the run file, then plan every work stage with its exact
prompt, **before the first dispatch**:

```sh
RM init TICKETS.md "drain the board" "B2+B3 books" "F2+F5 report, F3 cli" "verify review bump commit push"
printf '%s\n' "<the exact per-item prompts the script will send>" > .skillator/chain-66.txt
RM chain plan 66 --tickets "B2,B3" --fix build --verify build --files shelf/books.py --prompt-file .skillator/chain-66.txt
```

`init` printed the run's worktree (`stages work and commit in: ...`): every
prompt file says "work and commit in <worktree> (branch run/RUN-<n>-...),
never in the main checkout", and pastes this paragraph verbatim (A126 - a
background agent cannot ask for approval, so a command shape the host gates
is simply lost):

> In the worktree, run one plain command per call, by absolute path - never
> `cd` (or `Set-Location`) into it first. Git: `git -C "<worktree>" status`,
> `git -C "<worktree>" add <paths>`, `git -C "<worktree>" commit -m "..."`.
> Tests: `python -m pytest "<worktree>/tests"` (or the project's runner with
> the worktree path as its argument). No `&&` chains, no `$(...)`, no heredocs;
> read and edit files with the file tools, not shell redirection. The final stage merges that branch into main
from the main checkout, then removes the worktree and the branch. A `LEASED`
refusal (exit 2) means another run's stage holds one of this stage's files:
`chain next` lists it `IDLE <n> leased ...`; dispatch something else and come
back after that run lands. Ticket boxes are flipped with `RM board <ID> <mark>`
- the main checkout's board, under its lock.

`chain plan` allocates the 4-character code (`next-id.sh --runs .skillator W`),
prefixes it to the stage cell, and appends a block under `## Chain`. It refuses
without a prompt file and never reissues a code. Repeat for each work stage;
the final main-session stage needs no block. Without a Workflow tool, add
`--mode agents`.

Print the plan once — stages, codes, tickets, tiers, agent count, tickets left
out and why. A request that said "work the board in stages / keep going" is
the opt-in; "plan" stops here. No "shall I continue?" afterwards.

## Step 2 — dispatch a stage

Read usage first — before **every** dispatch, the first one included. A
reading the user gave in the prompt counts too; the higher of the two wins:

```sh
RM chain decide   # HOLD <pct> → step 4 now, dispatch nothing; RELEASE → go on
RM chain dispatch 66 --driver @cc-<6 chars of this session id> --owner build:opus
```

`dispatch` reads usage itself too. It refuses (exit 2) while `hold:` is set,
at or over the 5-hour hold without `--override` (the user asked; a ruling),
past the 7-day stop without `--confirmed`, while another driver's stamp is
under 20 minutes old (`--take` overrides, with a ruling), and on a stage that
is not pending or failed. `UNOBSERVABLE` dispatches, with a one-line note on
stderr. The checks and the claim are one lock hold: two sessions dispatching
one stage get one winner and one exit 2. On success it sets the row `~`,
copies the planned prompt verbatim into an In-flight block, and prints the code
and the prompt. Then:

1. Flip the stage's tickets to `[~]` with the session tag; grep them back.
2. Call `Workflow` with the `work-tickets` script shape from `tickets-zordon`;
   every fix and verify prompt carries the marathon.md paste-in paragraph,
   and the VERDICT schema its `parked` field.
   `meta.name: 'chain-<CODE>'`, every agent `label: '<CODE> fix:B2'` /
   `'<CODE> verify:B2'`, `args` = the items with tiers. **An F ticket's item is
   a `build-jarvis` pass** (F39), not a bare fix agent: its prompt opens with
   "Load skillator:build-jarvis" and the ticket, and build-jarvis grades,
   designs and builds it - B and A tickets keep the fix/verify shape.
3. Edit the In-flight block's `run: -` to the `runId` the tool returned — no
   command fills it. The prompt on disk is the truth; the id is a same-session
   hint for `resumeFromRunId`.

**Several in flight (F37).** `RM chain next --all` prints one `NEXT` line per
stage that can start now - its after: stages landed, its files disjoint from
every stage in flight and from the others it names, held by no decision and no
other run's lease - capped by usage: 2 below 50 % of the 5-hour window, 1 at or
above it or unobservable (`RELAY_CHAIN_PARALLEL` overrides). Dispatch each
(one dispatch and one Workflow/Agent call per stage). A stage left out says
why: `IDLE <n> slots`, `IDLE <n> parallel-files <m>`, `IDLE <n> inflight-files
<m>`; dispatch refuses a stage that shares files with one in flight, and one
with no `files:` never runs beside anything. A stage dispatched while another
is in flight gets its own worktree off the run branch - dispatch says so on
stderr and writes `worktree:`/`branch:` into its In-flight block; its prompt
must say to work and commit there. Each stage is landed by Step 3 when **its
own** notification arrives - the others keep running - and before its `stage x`
run `RM chain merge <n>`: it merges the stage branch into the run branch and
removes the stage worktree. Exit 3 is a conflict: the merge is aborted, the
stage is `!`, and a retry stage is planned on the merged branch. Then
`chain next --all` again fills the free slots.
`chain next --holds` (A118) prints only the `IDLE <n> Qk <why>` lines and
writes nothing - no lease beat, no lock - for readers such as holo-r2d2.

`mode:` in the Chain header names what actually ran: `workflow` for a Workflow
call, `agents` for Agent fan-out. A run file that says `workflow` while Agents
were used is a lie the next session believes — fix it with
`RM chain plan … --mode agents` at planning time, or by editing the header.

## Step 3 — between stages (the completion notification is the event)

Run every line, in order, before the next dispatch:

1. Read the returned array; read `<transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl` before
   believing an empty one. `null` → ticket stays `[~]`, said in the ruling.
   `passed:false` → `[ ]` with the `why` on the line. `passed:true` → `[x]`
   only when the evidence names a check that ran. The main session flips the
   board; no agent does. A verdict with `parked` → marathon.md (Park) first:
   `RM park` before anything else; `parked.stop` not `none` is a stop, now.
2. Regression sweep, then `code-review:code-review` on the staged diff; fix
   findings via a fix agent (3-pass cap). Usage pressure lowers the level,
   never the call: `/code-review low` is the floor. Reading the diff yourself
   is not a review - "to save usage I reviewed it myself" lands nothing.
3. Commit with the ticket-first message and the code trailing:
   `B2 B3: <what> [<CODE>]`. No review result from step 2, no `x`: the stage
   stays `~`. Then `RM stage 66 x build:opus <sha>` and delete
   the stage's In-flight block by hand (no command does). No passing ticket →
   `RM stage 66 '!'`, block kept with the failure appended, chain continues;
   one retry stage per ticket via `RM add`.
4. Republish the board artifact once (`tickets-zordon`).
5. `Ruling:` line — `<CODE>: <what the verdicts decided, what was dropped>;
   review <level>: <n> findings, <fixed|none>`.
6. Usage read, every stage, no exception:

   ```sh
   UW level        # src=<claude-code|codex|none> 5h=<pct|-> 7d=<pct|-> ctx=<pct|-> max=<pct|->
   RM chain decide # RELEASE <pct> | HOLD <pct> | HOLD <pct> 7d | UNOBSERVABLE
   ```

   `HOLD … 7d` → stop #4: `watch-cortana`'s 7-day order runs, and the hold is
   also written (step 4 below) so a resume knows why. `HOLD <pct>` → step 4.
   `UNOBSERVABLE` → say "usage: unobservable on this host" once in the plan,
   `usage: unobservable` in each ruling, and continue — no hold is possible.
7. Blocked re-check (step 1.2); a newly unblocked ticket → `RM add "<stage>"`,
   then `chain plan` it with its own prompt file.
8. Re-read the board; dropped or someone-else's `[~]` tickets leave the item
   list with a ruling. Then `RM chain next`: `NEXT` → step 2; `HOLD` → step 4;
   `ASK` / `UNBLOCK` → [marathon.md](marathon.md) (The end batch, Unblock)
   before anything final; `WAIT` → a stage is in flight, wait for its
   notification; `BLOCKED` → stages wait on a failed one: retry it (step 3.3)
   and close the failed row `>` naming the retry, or report it; `FINAL` → the
   main-session stage: review, version bump, commit; the push asks on its own,
   after the batch.

## Step 4 — the 80 % hold

```sh
RM chain hold 84 --window 5h --next 67       # writes `hold: <since> 84% 5h next=67`
```

Write it before arming anything; it is idempotent and keeps the first `since`.
Start nothing. On Claude Code arm the listener under the **Monitor** tool:

```sh
RM chain wait --for 1500                      # --for 540 in a -p / headless run
```

Exit 0 `RELEASE <pct>` → `RM chain release`, ruling, dispatch `next`.
Exit 5 `WAITING` → the arm's cap is spent; re-arm the same command.
Exit 3 `STUCK` → ruling, one more arm, then `AskUserQuestion` with the reading.
Exit 4 `UNOBSERVABLE` → release; the hold should never have been written.
Exit 2 `STOP <pct> 7d` → the 7-day window, not the 5-hour one: it will not refill
while you wait. Stop #4 — TaskStop the Monitor and hand off; a dispatch past it
needs `--confirmed`, never `--override`.
Hosts without Monitor record the hold, say "held at 84 %; say *next stage*, or
`continue RUN-<n>` later", and end the turn.

The hold is a wait, not a stop: no session handoff is written for it (that is
`watch-cortana`'s 92 % order). The threshold is `RELAY_CHAIN_HOLD_PCT` (80).

## Override — "next stage", "go on", "don't wait" while held

```sh
UW level
RM chain release --override                   # refused with exit 2 past 7d 90 %
```

Under the 7-day stop: TaskStop the Monitor, ruling `override: user asked at
<pct>%` (the command writes it), then `RM chain dispatch <n> … --override` —
dispatch re-reads usage, and the reading is still over 80 %. At or over 7-day 90 %:
`AskUserQuestion` — "7-day window at 91 % — the hard stop. Start <CODE>
anyway?" with *Hold (recommended — the window does not refill for days)* first.
Only the explicit yes runs `RM chain release --override --confirmed` and
`RM chain dispatch <n> … --confirmed`.

## Crash and resume

`RM list` (the SessionStart hook) names the run; `RM resume <id>` prints the
whole file, `## Chain` included. A `~` row is a stage that *started*: check the
tree, then redispatch from the In-flight prompt (or `resumeFromRunId` when the
id is this session's). `hold:` set → `UW level`; under → `RM chain release` and
dispatch `next`; over → `RM chain hold` again (same `since`) and arm the
listener. The driver's stamp is refreshed by its own `dispatch`, `heartbeat`,
`hold`, `release` and every `wait` poll, so a tag older than 20 minutes is a
driver that stopped, and may be taken.
Nothing is asked but the parked queue (`chain next` → `ASK`); the file is the plan.

1	# Marathon — park the user's questions, ask them all at the end
2	
3	## Entry — a marathon is picked, not assumed
4	
5	**A bare "work the board" or "work the open tickets" is a sweep, not a marathon
6	request.** With the user present, ask tickets-zordon's sweep mode question first
7	(Workflow mode, "Ask the mode once before a sweep"), with **marathon** offered
8	beside single / per-task / workflow: the staged chain on this page, which keeps
9	going across sessions and parks questions to one end batch.
10	
11	**Run a marathon without asking only when it was named** — `/marathon`,
12	"marathon", "keep going", "work them all, staged", "while I'm away" — or the run
13	is headless, chained or already inside a relay. Then log
14	`Ruling: mode marathon - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
15	
16	**Another mode picked → hand the tickets to tickets-zordon in that mode.** No
17	run is opened: no `init`, no `chain plan`.
18	
19	Every chain runs as a marathon unless the user said "ask me as you go"
20	(`RM queue --asks live`, then a parked question is asked at the next
21	between-stage point). Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-marathon.md`. `RM` is the same
22	page shorthand as in [chain.md](chain.md): type the full `sh "<path>" …` every
23	time. PowerShell: `-Mode park|answer|queue`, `-Mode chain -Action next|edge`.
24	
25	## Stops — never parked, asked now and alone
26	
27	```
28	A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION.
29	IT IS NEVER AN ITEM IN THE END BATCH.
30	```
31	
32	The six grayskull stops: a destructive or irreversible op, a security-sensitive
33	action, a side effect outside the worktree (push, merge, publish, message), the
34	7-day window at 90 %, a scope-contract breach, a failed repro. When one fires:
35	dispatch nothing new, end your message with that one question — what the act is,
36	that it cannot be undone, *Hold (recommended)* first — and nothing else in it.
37	The open queue is offered **after** the user has answered the stop, never beside
38	it. Two baseline runs saw that deleting untracked `data/legacy/` could not be
39	undone, said so, and still listed it as item 2 of 3 next to a format question:
40	a destructive op approved as one line of a batch is a rubber stamp. That is the
41	failure. "It's all questions for the same user" does not make a stop a decision;
42	`park` refuses `--stop` other than `none` (exit 2).
43	
44	Stops 5 and 6 are item-level by default (F31: the ticket fails `passed:false`,
45	never parked). The whole chain stops only when that ticket has dependants
46	(`after:`, `blocks:`, held files) or two repros fail in a row. The chain's own
47	push stays last, asked on its own after the unblock rounds.
48	
49	## Park — only what the user alone can decide
50	
51	All four, or it is a `Ruling:` with the default, as today:
52	1. **reason** `taste` (preference nothing settles), `fact` (only the user knows —
53	   *where* a credential lives, never its value) or `conflict` (ticket, spec and
54	   the user's words disagree and none binds);
55	2. not a stop;
56	3. two to four real options;
57	4. a default a ruling would pick.
58	
59	A park is the question written down **before** the next dispatch: park (disk) →
60	board flip (`[!] (blocked: RUN-n Qk - <8 words>)`, or split `F2a` done / `F2b`
61	blocked) → commit what passed → `RM stage <n> x|?` → ruling → `RM chain next`.
62	
63	```sh
64	RM park --stage 66 --ticket F2 --reason taste \
65	  --question "Should export write CSV or JSON by default?" --header Format \
66	  --option "JSON | matches list --json | breaks the spreadsheet habit" \
67	  --option "CSV | opens in Excel | needs a quoting rule" \
68	  --default JSON --recommended JSON --blocks "F2b, F5" \
69	  --files "shelf/export.py, tests/test_export.py" --done "F2a landed in AAQ7" --stop none
70	```
71	
72	It prints `Q<k>` (always quote it with the run: `RUN-11 Q2`). Planning-time
73	parks drop `--stage`. A repeat with the same stage and ticket prints the existing
74	Q and writes nothing, so replaying step 3 after a crash is safe. `park` refuses
75	(exit 2): no `## Chain`, fewer than 2 or more than 4 options, a missing
76	header/reason/default/files/stop, a header over 8 characters, a default that is
77	not an option, a line break, a `|` inside an option field, a field starting with
78	`#`, and key or token shapes (`sk-`, `ghp_`, 40+ hex — use the short sha).
79	
80	A stage where no item passed and one parked: nothing to commit, `RM stage <n>
81	'?'`, In-flight block kept with `parked: Q2` appended. Failed items get F31's one
82	retry stage. A park the verify agent judged not genuine: ruling with the
83	default, ticket `[ ]`, one retry stage.
84	
85	### Paste into every chain fix prompt
86	
87	> Before you edit, decide whether the ticket needs a choice only the user can
88	> make (taste, a fact only they know, a conflict nothing settles). If you can
89	> decide it from the ticket, spec, repo conventions or the user's words, decide
90	> it and say `Ruling:` in your report. If not: do every part that does not
91	> depend on the answer, and touch nothing that does. Do not stub it, guess it or
92	> leave a placeholder. Then end your report with `PARKED:` plus the question, 2–4
93	> options with what each does and where it hurts, your recommendation and
94	> default, the part that waits, and every file or directory it will touch (err
95	> wide). If the choice is a destructive, security or outside-the-worktree act,
96	> say `STOP:` instead. Never ask the user and never wait.
97	
98	Verify prompt addendum: *"If the report says PARKED: check that the independent
99	part works, check (git diff) that the gated files hold no partial guess, judge
100	whether the decision is genuinely the user's, and list every file the gated part
101	would touch; `parked.files` is the union of yours and the fixer's."* The VERDICT
102	schema gains one optional field:
103	
104	```js
105	parked: { type: 'object', properties: { question: {type:'string'}, header: {type:'string', maxLength: 8},
106	  options: {type:'array', minItems: 2, maxItems: 4, items: {type:'object', properties: {label:{type:'string'}, does:{type:'string'}, hurts:{type:'string'}}}},
107	  recommended: {type:'string'}, default: {type:'string'}, reason: {enum: ['taste','fact','conflict']},
108	  genuine: {type:'boolean'}, gated: {type:'string'}, files: {type:'array', minItems: 1, items: {type:'string'}},
109	  done: {type:'string'}, stop: {enum: ['none','destructive','security','outside','scope','repro']} },
110	  required: ['question','header','options','default','reason','genuine','gated','files','stop'] }
111	```
112	
113	`stop` other than `none` is not a park: handle it as that stop, now (above).
114	
115	## The loop — `chain next`
116	
117	Run it in place of "dispatch the next pending stage". It judges nothing:
118	
119	| Prints | Do |
120	|---|---|
121	| `NEXT <n> <CODE>` | dispatch it (chain.md Step 2) |
122	| `HOLD …` | chain.md Step 4 |
123	| `ASK <k>` | the end batch, below |
124	| `UNBLOCK Q<k>` (one line per Q) | Unblock, below — no question |
125	| `WAIT <k>` | k stages in flight, nothing else can start — wait for a notification |
126	| `BLOCKED <k>` | k stages wait (`after:`) on a failed one — retry it as a new stage, close the failed row `> stage <new>`, or report it |
127	| `FINAL` | the main-session stage; `- unanswered: …` lists Qs to name in the summary |
128	
129	`IDLE <n> Q<k> blocks|files|nofiles|after` lines say why a stage waits. A Q
130	holds while `open`, `asked`, `answered` or `ruled`; it stops only at `replanned`
131	or `moot`. A stage with no `files:` waits while any Q holds. `chain dispatch`
132	refuses a stage idle on a Q or on an `after:` stage not landed, a `?` stage, and
133	`chain next` never offers a `!` row (retry = a new stage via `RM add`). A `>` row
134	counts as landed once the stage it names has. An edge found late:
135	`RM chain edge <n> --after 66` or `--independent-of Q2 --why "<ruling>"`.
136	
137	The hold gates dispatch, not questions: under a hold `ASK` and `UNBLOCK` still
138	print. A user who types mid-run while work can dispatch gets one line —
139	"2 decisions parked, asked at the end" — not the batch.

# Marathon — park the user's questions, ask them all at the end

## Entry — a marathon is picked, not assumed

**A bare "work the board" or "work the open tickets" is a sweep, not a marathon
request.** With the user present, ask tickets-zordon's sweep mode question first
(Workflow mode, "Ask the mode once before a sweep"), with **marathon** offered
beside single / per-task / workflow: the staged chain on this page, which keeps
going across sessions and parks questions to one end batch.

**Run a marathon without asking only when it was named** — `/marathon`,
"marathon", "keep going", "work them all, staged", "while I'm away" — or the run
is headless, chained or already inside a relay. Then log
`Ruling: mode marathon - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.

**Another mode picked → hand the tickets to tickets-zordon in that mode.** No
run is opened: no `init`, no `chain plan`.

Every chain runs as a marathon unless the user said "ask me as you go"
(`RM queue --asks live`, then a parked question is asked at the next
between-stage point). Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-marathon.md`. `RM` is the same
page shorthand as in [chain.md](chain.md): type the full `sh "<path>" …` every
time. PowerShell: `-Mode park|answer|queue`, `-Mode chain -Action next|edge`.

## Stops — never parked, asked now and alone

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION.
IT IS NEVER AN ITEM IN THE END BATCH.
```

The six grayskull stops: a destructive or irreversible op, a security-sensitive
action, a side effect outside the worktree (push, merge, publish, message), the
7-day window at 90 %, a scope-contract breach, a failed repro. When one fires:
dispatch nothing new, end your message with that one question — what the act is,
that it cannot be undone, *Hold (recommended)* first — and nothing else in it.
The open queue is offered **after** the user has answered the stop, never beside
it. Two baseline runs saw that deleting untracked `data/legacy/` could not be
undone, said so, and still listed it as item 2 of 3 next to a format question:
a destructive op approved as one line of a batch is a rubber stamp. That is the
failure. "It's all questions for the same user" does not make a stop a decision;
`park` refuses `--stop` other than `none` (exit 2).

Stops 5 and 6 are item-level by default (F31: the ticket fails `passed:false`,
never parked). The whole chain stops only when that ticket has dependants
(`after:`, `blocks:`, held files) or two repros fail in a row. The chain's own
push stays last, asked on its own after the unblock rounds.

## Park — only what the user alone can decide

All four, or it is a `Ruling:` with the default, as today:
1. **reason** `taste` (preference nothing settles), `fact` (only the user knows —
   *where* a credential lives, never its value) or `conflict` (ticket, spec and
   the user's words disagree and none binds);
2. not a stop;
3. two to four real options;
4. a default a ruling would pick.

A park is the question written down **before** the next dispatch: park (disk) →
board flip (`[!] (blocked: RUN-n Qk - <8 words>)`, or split `F2a` done / `F2b`
blocked) → commit what passed → `RM stage <n> x|?` → ruling → `RM chain next`.

```sh
RM park --stage 66 --ticket F2 --reason taste \
  --question "Should export write CSV or JSON by default?" --header Format \
  --option "JSON | matches list --json | breaks the spreadsheet habit" \
  --option "CSV | opens in Excel | needs a quoting rule" \
  --default JSON --recommended JSON --blocks "F2b, F5" \
  --files "shelf/export.py, tests/test_export.py" --done "F2a landed in AAQ7" --stop none
```

It prints `Q<k>` (always quote it with the run: `RUN-11 Q2`). Planning-time
parks drop `--stage`. A repeat with the same stage and ticket prints the existing
Q and writes nothing, so replaying step 3 after a crash is safe. `park` refuses
(exit 2): no `## Chain`, fewer than 2 or more than 4 options, a missing
header/reason/default/files/stop, a header over 8 characters, a default that is
not an option, a line break, a `|` inside an option field, a field starting with
`#`, and key or token shapes (`sk-`, `ghp_`, 40+ hex — use the short sha).

A stage where no item passed and one parked: nothing to commit, `RM stage <n>
'?'`, In-flight block kept with `parked: Q2` appended. Failed items get F31's one
retry stage. A park the verify agent judged not genuine: ruling with the
default, ticket `[ ]`, one retry stage.

### Paste into every chain fix prompt

> Before you edit, decide whether the ticket needs a choice only the user can
> make (taste, a fact only they know, a conflict nothing settles). If you can
> decide it from the ticket, spec, repo conventions or the user's words, decide
> it and say `Ruling:` in your report. If not: do every part that does not
> depend on the answer, and touch nothing that does. Do not stub it, guess it or
> leave a placeholder. Then end your report with `PARKED:` plus the question, 2–4
> options with what each does and where it hurts, your recommendation and
> default, the part that waits, and every file or directory it will touch (err
> wide). If the choice is a destructive, security or outside-the-worktree act,
> say `STOP:` instead. Never ask the user and never wait.

Verify prompt addendum: *"If the report says PARKED: check that the independent
part works, check (git diff) that the gated files hold no partial guess, judge
whether the decision is genuinely the user's, and list every file the gated part
would touch; `parked.files` is the union of yours and the fixer's."* The VERDICT
schema gains one optional field:

```js
parked: { type: 'object', properties: { question: {type:'string'}, header: {type:'string', maxLength: 8},
  options: {type:'array', minItems: 2, maxItems: 4, items: {type:'object', properties: {label:{type:'string'}, does:{type:'string'}, hurts:{type:'string'}}}},
  recommended: {type:'string'}, default: {type:'string'}, reason: {enum: ['taste','fact','conflict']},
  genuine: {type:'boolean'}, gated: {type:'string'}, files: {type:'array', minItems: 1, items: {type:'string'}},
  done: {type:'string'}, stop: {enum: ['none','destructive','security','outside','scope','repro']} },
  required: ['question','header','options','default','reason','genuine','gated','files','stop'] }
```

`stop` other than `none` is not a park: handle it as that stop, now (above).

## The loop — `chain next`

Run it in place of "dispatch the next pending stage". It judges nothing:

| Prints | Do |
|---|---|
| `NEXT <n> <CODE>` | dispatch it (chain.md Step 2) |
| `HOLD …` | chain.md Step 4 |
| `ASK <k>` | the end batch, below |
| `UNBLOCK Q<k>` (one line per Q) | Unblock, below — no question |
| `WAIT <k>` | k stages in flight, nothing else can start — wait for a notification |
| `BLOCKED <k>` | k stages wait (`after:`) on a failed one — retry it as a new stage, close the failed row `> stage <new>`, or report it |
| `FINAL` | the main-session stage; `- unanswered: …` lists Qs to name in the summary |

`IDLE <n> Q<k> blocks|files|nofiles|after` lines say why a stage waits. A Q
holds while `open`, `asked`, `answered` or `ruled`; it stops only at `replanned`
or `moot`. A stage with no `files:` waits while any Q holds. `chain dispatch`
refuses a stage idle on a Q or on an `after:` stage not landed, a `?` stage, and
`chain next` never offers a `!` row (retry = a new stage via `RM add`). A `>` row
counts as landed once the stage it names has. An edge found late:
`RM chain edge <n> --after 66` or `--independent-of Q2 --why "<ruling>"`.

The hold gates dispatch, not questions: under a hold `ASK` and `UNBLOCK` still
print. A user who types mid-run while work can dispatch gets one line —
"2 decisions parked, asked at the end" — not the batch.

## The end batch

1. **Re-validate** each open Q: its ticket closed, or a landed stage settled it →
   `RM answer Qk --moot "<why>"`. **Deduplicate**: the later of two parks of one
   question → `RM answer Qk --same-as Qj` (its blocks and files join Qj).
2. `RM queue` prints the batch, most-blocked first, chips cut to 8.
   **Draw it** before asking - one command, `node <skills>/holo-r2d2/scripts/holo.mjs
   RUN-<n> --batch`: it writes the page, the standalone page and the decision
   wizard and prints the ASCII picture with every path. **Paste that whole
   output above the questions**, every time - the picture is part of the
   batch, not an extra. With the Artifact tool, also publish the
   `.artifact.html` it names (private, `capabilities: {db: {}}`). The
   wizard's finalized JSON becomes `RM answer` lines (`holo.mjs --answers <file>`).
3. **AskUserQuestion in your tool list** (interactive Claude Code): pages of up to
   4 questions × 4 options, back to back, no dispatch between. Header = the chip
   as-is; question text `RUN-11 Q7 (2/3): <question>`; option 1 is the
   recommended one; description "does · hurts". The first page's first
   question text ends `- drawn: <link or path>`. After **each** page, before the
   next: `RM answer Qk "<label or the user's own words>"`; "you decide" →
   `--ruled`. Unanswered or dismissed → leave it; it is not asked again this
   marathon.
4. **No AskUserQuestion** (`-p`, Codex, Cursor, agents): `RM queue --mark-asked`,
   the `--batch` output (picture and paths) above its list as the one message,
   run FINAL on what landed, end the turn.
   The reply (same session or `continue RUN-n`) becomes `RM answer` calls,
   written before any dispatch, then Unblock and a second FINAL.

Never prose asking "what do you want?" — the queue's list is the shape.

## Unblock — re-plan, never re-dispatch

For each `UNBLOCK Qk`, while it still holds:
1. Collect the `[!]` tickets and `b`-parts in its `blocks:` **and every stage

2. Tickets → `[ ]`. `RM add` a new stage, write a **new** prompt that quotes the

3. Each collected old row → `RM stage <old> '>' - "stage <new>"`; or keep it
   under `RM chain edge <old> --independent-of Qk --why …`. Default: re-plan.
4. `RM answer Qk --replanned <new>`. Ruling:
   `Q2: CSV - replanned as stage 71 (AAQB); stage 70 (F5) replanned as 72`.

## A marathon of runs (F38)

Several runs wait their turn in one queue, `<main>/.skillator/queue.md`:

```sh

RM queue-run next          # START RUN-0012 | BUSY RUN-0012 running | DONE
RM queue-run start 12      # then `continue RUN-0012` - its chain runs as above

```

halts everything.

**Landing** - one run at a time, on main, never pushed:

1. `RM land <n> --start` - rebases the run branch onto main in the run's

import sys

from shelf.cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Ikran\AppData\Local\Temp\f52\put-green\skills\build-jarvis

# build-jarvis — every feature, graded, designed, built

The one build skill. It **is** `PRACTICE.md` §§1-6 for a feature, design
included, so nothing runs in front of it — not `superpowers:brainstorming`, not
`writing-plans`, not a second `build-*`. You are the **orchestrator**: you grade,
dispatch, rule and keep the record. Design and code run in subagents, each with
an explicit model, because a skill cannot change the main session's model.

Read **`PRACTICE.md`** first — beside `PLATFORMS.md`, at the plugin root (`../`
in the `install.sh` layout, `../../` in a checkout or the plugin cache). It owns
classification, questions, the TASKS shape, self-review, test-first, evidence
and review. Everything below assumes it.

## Step 0 — GRADE, before anything is spent

1. **Classify** spike / bounded / architectural (PRACTICE §1).
2. **Criticality.** The work is **critical** when it touches auth, money,
   concurrency, or a contract others depend on (a shared API, a file format, a
   schema). Say which word made it critical.
3. **Tier each seat** from this table — the same one as `practice/task-loop.md`
   § Model selection and `tickets-zordon`'s scout:

   | The work reads like | design | build | verify |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | One file, mechanical, the change is named | — | cheap | build |
   | 1-2 files, complete spec, nothing left to decide | — | cheap | build |
   | Several files, integration, or choices left open | deep | build | build |
   | Cause unknown, design judgement, architectural | deep | build | deep |
   | Critical (any row) | deep | build | **deep, held** |

   Critical's build seat is the **build** tier (`build=opus` on Claude Code,
   per `PLATFORMS.md`), never cheap.

   `—` = no design pass: the request or ticket *is* the spec, and you write it
   into the design file as its one task. **build is the floor** for every verify
   seat and for a build seat working from prose rather than named code.
4. **Tier → model:** read `.skillator/tiers.local.md` (written by
   `grayskull-power`'s `tiers` arm step). Missing → the first slug in your
   host's column of `PLATFORMS.md` § Role tiers, and say `tiers: defaults`.
5. **Step down, never up on your own** — the one exception is Phase 2's
   third fix round, and only with its `Ruling:` line:
   - a tier whose model the file marks `down:` → that seat goes one tier lower;
   - usage ≥ 70 % of the 5-hour window (`watch-cortana`'s `usage-watch.* level`,
     the `5h=` field) → every **non-critical** seat one tier lower; `src=none`
     → no step-down, and say `usage unobservable`;
   - never below cheap, never a verify seat below build, and a **held** seat
     keeps the highest tier still available.
   Every downgrade is a line: `Ruling: <seat> <from>-><to> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
6. **User words win over the table** (unavailability still wins over them):
   "use fable" / "fable designs" → design and deep seats on fable · "opus only"
   / "all opus" → every seat opus · "cheap" / "on a budget" → every
   non-critical seat one tier lower · "top tier" / "best models" → every seat
   deep · a named model → that seat on it.
7. **Your first reply text after loading this skill is the grade line** —
   before the design-file Write, before any Agent call. No confirmation gate
   (step 8's mode question is the one Step 0 ask); the line is there so the
   user can overrule before the first token is spent:

   ```
   grade: bounded · critical no · design - · build cheap=sonnet · verify build=opus · ceremony lean · mode ask (single) · usage 5h 41%
   ```

   **Printed means reply text the user sees**, starting `grade:`, before the
   design file is written or anything is dispatched. A grade worked out in your
   thinking, a `Ruling: critical no` in the design file, or a summary at the
   end is not printed — the user cannot overrule a line they never saw.

   **The line is a required input.** It is the design file's first line and
   the first line of every Agent prompt (design, build, verify), verbatim. So
   whichever spend comes first — the design-file Write *or* a design agent —
   print the line as reply text, then paste the same line into that call.
8. **Mode — the grade line's `mode` field, settled before any spend.** How
   Phase 2 runs:

   | Mode | What runs | Fits |
   |---|---|---|
   | **single** | One build agent does every task in order; design and verify stay their own seats | `—` design seat, 1-3 tightly coupled tasks, tasks sharing files |
   | **per-task** | One fresh build agent per task (`tasks-sentinels`); same-file tasks never fan out | Several independent tasks — the usual pick when nothing else fits |
   | **workflow** | Phases 1-3 as one workflow script (`WORKFLOW.md`); no `Workflow` tool → the host's parallel subagents | 4+ independent tasks or a sweep — costs the most tokens |

   - `mode ask (<recommended>)` — the default. Right after the grade line, ask
     once: all three modes, your recommendation first (`AskUserQuestion`; no
     such tool → a numbered list). Then **end your turn** — no design-file
     Write, no Agent, until the user answers. Then reprint the line with
     `mode <m> (asked)`; that line is the one the design file and every
     Agent prompt carry.
   - `mode <m> (named)` — the user already named one ("single agent", "one
     agent per task", "use a workflow", "ultracode"). No question.
   - `mode <m> (ruled)` — the prompt or run says headless, chained or inside a
     relay. No question; log `Ruling: mode <m> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
     A bare feature request is not headless, whatever tools you lack.

   Recommend from the grade row and how coupled the work reads. **Never
   workflow without the user's opt-in**: unasked, the most you pick is per-task.

**Ceremony** is `full` when the work is architectural, has 4+ tasks, runs
inside a relay run, or is said to outlive this session ("keep going after",
"hand it over", "full ceremony"); otherwise `lean`. Full adds the session
record, the handoff checkpoint, the TRACE table and the rework loop —
**[references/ceremony.md](references/ceremony.md)**.

Grade detail, the tiers file, the unavailable-at-dispatch retry and worked
examples: **[references/grade.md](references/grade.md)**.

## Design questions — ruled or parked, never asked mid-build

- **Decidable** from the repo, the ticket, PRACTICE or a stated rule → rule it
  and write it into the design file's `## Decisions`:
  `Ruling: <what> - <why> - <cost if wrong>`.
- **Only the user can answer** (taste, a fact only they hold, a conflict nothing
  settles) → `relay-morpheus park`, and build everything that does not depend on
  it. A relay run in flight → park on its stage. A standalone build → open a
  one-stage run first so the park has a home (commands in
  [references/grade.md](references/grade.md#parking-from-a-standalone-build)).
- **The six stops** (destructive op, security-sensitive action, a side effect
  outside this worktree, the 7-day limit at 90 %, a scope breach, a failed
  repro) → ask now, alone.
- **Architectural** keeps PRACTICE §1's one approval gate after the design is
  written and reviewed — asked when the user is present, parked when the run is
  headless, chained or the user is away.
- "ask me as you go", "brainstorm with me", "let's design it together" →
  live questions instead, one at a time (PRACTICE §1); each answer still lands
  in `## Decisions`.

## Phase 1 — Design

Design seat `—` → write the design file yourself from the request. Otherwise
dispatch one design agent on the design seat's model with the request verbatim,
the repo context and `PRACTICE.md`; it writes the file and returns only its path
plus two lines:

```
grade: <the Step 0 line, verbatim - also already printed as reply text>
GOAL:         <the task in one line>
CHOSEN:       <the approach + why; architectural lists 2-3 APPROACHES first>
DESIGN:       <data model / contracts, key edge cases, out of scope>
CONSTRAINTS:  <what stays true across every task - exact values, names,
              formats; copied verbatim into every reviewer as
              [GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS]>
TASKS:        <one block per task in PRACTICE §2 shape (Files, Interfaces,
              test-first steps with real code and commands), each tagged
              build=<tier> from the Step 0 table>
VERIFICATION: <the exact end-to-end command and its expected output>
## Decisions  <every Ruling: made so far; parked questions by Q-id>
```

Lean: `design-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` in the scratchpad. Full:
`docs/sessions/session-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`, plus the REQUIREMENTS / TRACE
slots in [references/ceremony.md](references/ceremony.md). Then self-review it
(PRACTICE §3) and fix inline. A **spike** stops at Phase 1: the probe and a
recommendation, nothing kept.

## Phase 2 — Build

The Step 0.8 mode decides the shape. **per-task**: one agent per task, each on
its own tagged tier; independent tasks fan out, same-file tasks do not.
**single**: one build agent takes every task block in order, on the highest
tagged tier, and reports per block. Either way a build agent gets fresh context,
the **design file path** and its task block(s) — never the design pasted, never
this session's history (PRACTICE §4; procedure `practice/task-loop.md`, prompt
text `practice/prompts.md`). Several F tickets are one pass, one task block per
ticket; a build agent implements its block(s) only — it never loads this skill,
regrades or runs its own verify. Review each block against its spec before the
next dispatch; a failed review goes to a fix agent. A third round may go one
tier up, and only with
`Ruling: <seat> <from>-><to> - reviews <1> and <2> failed: <why each failed> - <cost if wrong>`
citing both failed reviews; no Ruling, no step up.

**Mode workflow** (the user opted in) → run Phases 1-3 as one workflow script
(`WORKFLOW.md`): write the design file first, pass its path in `args`, and the
build stage reads each task's tier: `model: M[t.build]`.

## Phase 3 — Verify, review, relay

Run VERIFICATION through PRACTICE §5 — the command, now, in full, exit code
read — on the verify seat. Anything bigger than bounded, or critical, gets one
whole-diff review on the verify seat's tier (PRACTICE §6,
`code-review:code-review`). Failures go back through Phase 2's fix loop. Then
relay: the grade line again as the report's first line, what was built
(files), the verification evidence, every Ruling, every parked Q-id.

## Rules

- **Grade before spending.** No design file, no dispatch, before the grade
  line is printed as reply text.
- **A budget is a step-down, never a merge.** A spend cap (`--max-budget-usd`,
  "on a budget", a cost ceiling) means "cheap" — every non-critical seat one
  tier lower, said in a `Ruling:`. It never reaches critical work: critical
  keeps its deep design seat (a dispatched design agent) and its deep, held
  verify. It never folds the seats into this session:
  a subagent costs no more than the same work done here, and the orchestrator
  that builds has nobody to verify it.

| Rationalization | Reality |
|---|---|
| "I graded it — it's in my reasoning / the design file's Rulings." | Not printed. The line exists so the user can overrule it before spend; invisible, it overrules nothing. |
| "Small and obvious; the grade line is ceremony." | It is one line. Size does not waive it; `design -` already says it was small. |
| "The budget won't cover subagents, so I'll design, build and verify here." | Same tokens, minus the second pair of eyes. Step seats down; keep them separate. |
| "Critical work — safer if I do it all myself." | Critical makes verify **deep, held**: a different seat, not this one. |
| "The cap reads as cheap, so the critical design seat drops to build." | The step-down is for non-critical seats only. Critical design stays deep and dispatched. |

**Red flag:** about to Write the design file, or call Agent — a design agent
included — with no `grade:` line in your reply text yet, or with `mode ask`
still unanswered: stop and print or ask first. Critical work is no exception;
it is where the overrule matters most.
- **Never an unnamed model.** An omitted model inherits the session's.
- **The design file is the handover.** Pass it by path; the orchestrator does
  not design or code, bar writing a `—`-seat design file and the record.
- **Autonomous, honest.** A phase that fails or an agent that returns nothing is
  said plainly; nothing continues on a missing piece.
- **Handoff before context loss.** About to `/compact` or `/clear` → run
  `handoff-cortana` first.

## Other hosts

`PLATFORMS.md` turns tiers into slugs and dispatch into the host's delegate
mechanism; no delegation → run the seats sequentially in one session, each
phase's output written to disk before the model switch. Per-host notes, the
seat table and the Opus-version limit: [references/platforms.md](references/platforms.md).
The `UserPromptSubmit` route hook that puts a feature prompt here on Claude
Code: [references/route-hook.md](references/route-hook.md).
